research_question: What is the effect of behavioural support, compared with brief advice or no intervention, on tobacco use cessation?
control_label: Brief advice or no intervention (with matched pharmacotherapy where applicable)
outcome_description: Tobacco use cessation rate (abstinence from smoking/tobacco)
positive_direction: Higher cessation rates (greater abstinence) in the behavioural support group compared to the control group
search_queries: behavioural support smoking cessation randomized trial
behavioral counseling tobacco cessation controlled comparison
behavioural intervention tobacco abstinence trial effect
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies examining behavioural support interventions for smoking or tobacco use cessation
Studies comparing behavioural support (with or without matched pharmacotherapy) against brief advice, usual care, or minimal/no intervention
Reporting quantitative cessation or abstinence rates or related tobacco use cessation measures
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, protocols, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers are excluded)
No comparison between a behavioural support intervention and a brief advice or control condition
No quantitative cessation or abstinence outcome data available to calculate an effect size
Completely unrelated to tobacco use cessation or behavioural support
moderators_to_extract: Intervention combination subgroup (behavioural support alone, behavioural support + NRT, behavioural support + varenicline)
Behavioural support delivery modality (individual counseling, group therapy, telephone support, digital/text)
Control condition type (brief advice, usual care, self-help, no intervention)
Biochemical verification of abstinence (verified vs self-report only)
Follow-up duration of cessation assessment (e.g., 6 months, 12 months)
effect_size_note: For trials testing multiple behavioural support variants against a single shared control arm, divide the control group sample size and event count proportionally across comparisons to prevent double-counting of control participants. Subgroups are structured by co-intervention: behavioural support alone vs brief advice/control; behavioural support + NRT vs brief advice/control + NRT; and behavioural support + varenicline vs varenicline alone.
